hello.note: Also used for goodbye. Casual: היי (hai).

please.note: Also used for 'here you go' and as a reply to thanks.

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: תודה רבה (toda raba).

sorry.note: A woman says: מצטערת (mitsta'eret). For small slips, סליחה (slicha) is enough.

how_are_you.note: To a woman: ma shlomech (same spelling). Casual: מה נשמע? (ma nishma?)

whats_your_name.note: To a woman: eich kor'im lach? (same spelling).

nice_to_meet_you.note: Common reply: גם לי (gam li), 'me too'.

where_from.note: To a woman: מאיפה את? (me'eifo at?)

im_from.note: מ (mi-; me- before א, ה, ע, ר) is joined to the country: אני מקנדה (ani mikanada), מאנגליה (me'anglia).

speak_english.note: To a woman: את מדברת אנגלית? (at medaberet anglit?)

dont_understand.note: A woman says: אני לא מבינה (ani lo mevina).

speak_slowly.note: אפשר (efshar) + verb is a polite request that works for anyone, man or woman.

where_bathroom.note: Start with סליחה (slicha) to be polite.

can_you_help.note: To a woman: את יכולה לעזור לי? (at yechola la'azor li?)

one.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: אחד (echad).

two.note: Counting form. Masculine: שניים (shnayim). Right before a noun: שתי / שני (shtei / shnei).

three.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: שלושה (shlosha).

four.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: ארבעה (arba'a).

five.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: חמישה (chamisha).

six.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: שישה (shisha).

seven.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: שבעה (shiv'a).

eight.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: shmona (same spelling).

nine.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: תשעה (tish'a).

ten.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: עשרה (asara).

water.note: A glass of water: כוס מים (kos mayim).

coffee.note: The Israeli milky coffee (like a latte) is הפוך (hafuch).

im_hungry.note: A woman says: אני רעבה (ani re'eva).

no_meat.note: A woman says: אני לא אוכלת בשר (ani lo ochelet basar).

stop_here.note: To a woman driver: תעצרי פה, בבקשה (ta'atsri po, bevakasha).

airport.note: Ben Gurion Airport is usually just called נתב״ג (natbag).

want_to_go.note: A woman says ani rotsa (same spelling). ל (le-) is joined to the place: לחיפה (lecheifa).

one_ticket.note: Most buses and trains take the רב-קו (rav-kav) smart card instead.

id_like_this.note: A woman says ani rotsa (same spelling). Also: אני אקח את זה (ani ekach et ze), 'I'll take it'.

just_looking.note: A woman says: אני רק מסתכלת, תודה (ani rak mistakelet, toda).

pay_card.note: אשראי (ashrai), literally 'credit', is everyday shorthand for a credit card. בכרטיס (bekartis), 'by card', also works.

see_you_later.note: Also: נתראה אחר כך (nitra'e achar kach).

wait_moment.note: Or: חכה רגע (chake rega); to a woman: חכי רגע (chaki rega).

call_police.note: Plural, shouted to everyone around. Police emergency number in Israel: 100.

need_doctor.note: A woman says: אני צריכה רופא (ani tsricha rofe). Ambulance (Magen David Adom): 101.

dont_feel_well.note: A woman says: אני לא מרגישה טוב (ani lo margisha tov).

lost_phone.note: A mobile phone is also commonly called פלאפון (pelefon).

allergic.note: A woman says: אני אלרגית ל… (ani alergit le…).

be_careful.note: To a woman: תיזהרי! (tizahari!). Also: זהירות! (zehirut!)

dont_know.note: A woman says: אני לא יודעת (ani lo yoda'at).

i_like_it.note: A woman says ani ohevet (אוהבת). Also: זה מוצא חן בעיניי (ze motse chen be'einai).

dont_like_it.note: A woman says: אני לא אוהבת את זה (ani lo ohevet et ze).

im_tired.note: A woman says: אני עייפה (ani ayefa).

im_happy.note: A woman says: אני שמחה (ani smecha).

welcome.note: To a woman: ברוכה הבאה (brucha haba'a); to a group: ברוכים הבאים (bruchim haba'im).

congratulations.note: For an achievement, Israelis often say כל הכבוד (kol hakavod).
